note: This catches common problems. It isn't legal advice, and your broker's rules come first.
about: The check before posting (design §3.13), read by shared/compliance.js. Word lists are English and conservative: HUD withdrew its 1995 advertising memo and its 2024 digital-ad guidance, but the Fair Housing Act and 24 CFR 100.75 are unchanged. Patterns are JavaScript regular expressions (matched case-insensitively unless "case": true); "replace" is the one-tap fix ($1 = the first group, "" = take the words out); a phrase without "replace" is flagged without a one-tap fix, or with "remove": true takes out the sentence. "except" lists near misses that must stay quiet.

fh.people.why: The Fair Housing Act's rule on ads (24 CFR 100.75) bars words that "convey that dwellings are available or not available to a particular group"; HUD's 1995 guidance named a preference "for adults, couples or singles". Describe the home instead (NAR's examples: "4 bedrooms, fenced yard", "single-story").
fh.people.fixLabel: Say what the home has, not who should live there

phrases.label: Take it out and name the features (4 bedrooms, fenced yard)

fh.protected.why: The same rule (24 CFR 100.75) covers race, color, religion, sex, disability, familial status and national origin; Florida's Fair Housing Act has the same classes. Describe the property and the amenities, never the people who live there or should.
fh.protected.fixLabel: Take out the sentence; describe the property and the amenities

fh.safe.why: "Safe" and "exclusive" are subjective and can read as steering; fair housing guides offer the feature instead (a gated community, lit walking paths) or leaving it out.
fh.safe.fixLabel: Name the feature instead, or leave it out

fh.schools.why: Factual school details are fine, but an unnamed "great schools" reads as a preference, and zoning varies by address. Name the school with its state grade and year ("Lake Mary High, an A school in 2026"), and only say a home is zoned for a school when you've checked that address.

phrases.text: Check the zoning: '{match}' a school varies by address

fh.places.why: Conservative state guidance (Indiana's civil rights commission) avoids "near churches" and "walking distance": say "near places of worship", "convenient to" or "5 minutes from".

phrases.re: \b(?:near|close to|next to|steps from|minutes from|around the corner from)\s+(?:a\s+|the\s+|several\s+|many\s+|lots of\s+)?(?:churches|church|synagogues?|mosques?|temples?)\b

fh.primary.why: "Master bedroom" is legal (HUD's 1995 guidance cleared it), but most MLSs and many brokers now prefer "primary".

fl.brokerage.why: Florida Rule 61J2-10.025: "All real estate advertisements must include the licensed name of the brokerage firm", online beside the contact information. The rule predates social media, so the safe practice is the name on every promotional post and in your bio.
fl.brokerage.textNoBrokerage: Add your brokerage's licensed name in You, so the check can look for it
fl.brokerage.fixLabel: Add "{brokerage}" as the caption's last line

num.unsourced.why: NAR Code of Ethics, Article 12: advertising must present a true picture. Nobody supplied this number, so it may be wrong: take it out, or check it and add its source.

num.source.why: NAR Code of Ethics, Article 12 (a true picture): a statistic goes with its source and period. MLS-based numbers say "Based on information from Stellar MLS for <period>".

promise.why: NAR Code of Ethics, Article 12 (a true picture): nobody can promise appreciation, prices or rates. Say what the data shows instead.

phrases.re: \b(?:homes?|houses?|propert(?:y|ies)|condos?|values?|home values|prices?|it|investment|market)\s+(?:will|is going to|are going to|is gonna|are gonna)\s+(?:definitely\s+|certainly\s+|surely\s+|only\s+|always\s+|keep\s+)?(?:appreciate|appreciating|go up|going up|rise|rising|increase|gain value|double|skyrocket|be worth more)\b

\b(?:prices|values|home values|rates|mortgage rates|interest rates)\s+(?:will|are going to|are gonna)\s+(?:definitely\s+|certainly\s+|surely\s+)?(?:go up|rise|increase|drop|fall|come down|go down|double|skyrocket|crash)\b

regz.why: Truth in Lending (Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.24(d)): a payment amount, a down payment or a number of payments in an ad for home credit is a "trigger term" that requires the down payment, the repayment terms and the APR. Take it out, or use your lender's disclosed example.
regz.text: Payment terms need the full disclosure: '{match}'

copy.why: NAR Standard of Practice 12-10: no "content developed by others without either attribution or without permission". Borrow the format, never the words.

politics.why: Your brand works for every client: explain a ballot measure (what it does and what each side says), never how to vote, and leave candidates and parties out.
politics.tweakNote: Make it a neutral explainer: what it does and what each side says, never how to vote; no candidates or parties.

phrases.re: \b(?:Byron Donalds|David Jolly|Jay Collins|Ashley Moody|Jason Pizzo|Kamala Harris|J\.?D\.? Vance|Casey DeSantis)\b

music.why: TikTok: businesses "cannot use the general music library for commercial usage" (its Commercial Music Library is the way); Meta: commercial use of music "is prohibited unless you have obtained appropriate licenses".
music.replace: Original audio, or a sound marked for business use

lang.why: The word lists are English. The numbers and the brokerage checks still ran.
lang.text: Word check is English-only: read it over once.

fl.team.why: Florida Rule 61J2-10.026: a team may call itself a "team" or "group" but not "Realty", "Real Estate", "Properties", "Brokers" or "LLC", and the team name may never be larger than the brokerage's, so the app always shows the brokerage with it.
fl.team.textNoBrokerage: Add your brokerage's name: it always goes with the team name
